unexecuted_proposal.brief_basis: Chart_1 labeled rating shares: Quality 24%, Price 10%, Design 52%, Support 45%, Delivery 39%, Other 32%. Design has the highest labeled rating share (52%), so the follow-up category is Design. The form is on the form page with no selection yet; selecting Design is the first required step before filling companion fields and submitting.

rules.text: If the chart's printed percentage labels are treated as the authoritative 'labeled rating share' values, then the category whose label is numerically greatest is the one with the highest current labeled rating share, and the corresponding public option label is the required follow-up category.
rules.conditions: Assumes the printed percentage inscriptions are the intended rating-share values and that the public option labels map one-to-one to the chart categories.

rules.text: If the chart's vertical axis position (Value) is treated as the authoritative rating-share value instead of the printed labels, then the category whose point is highest on the page is the one with the highest current rating share, and the corresponding public option label is the required follow-up category.
rules.conditions: Assumes the y-axis 'Value' scale is the intended rating-share measure and that the printed percentage labels are decorative or inconsistent with the axis.

rules.text: If the public task requires selecting a category from the provided option_labels, then any chart category that does not appear in option_labels cannot be selected, and the highest-share category must be chosen from among the available options only.
rules.conditions: Assumes the option_labels list is exhaustive for the primary field and that no other category can be entered.

chains.claim: If the y-axis 'Value' position is the intended measure rather than the printed labels, Quality's mark at ~60 is highest on the page, not Design's at ~42. This creates a visible conflict between the printed label (Design 52%) and the axis geometry (Quality ~60), leaving the 'labeled rating share' interpretation open to challenge if the axis is considered authoritative.

The chart contains six categories (Quality, Price, Design, Support, Delivery, Other), but the public option_labels only include Design, Quality, and Support. If the highest-share category were Price, Delivery, or Other under any interpretation, it could not be selected. Under the label-based reading, Design is available; under the axis-based reading, Quality is available. The constraint does not resolve the conflict but confirms that only Design, Quality, or Support can be the final selection.

questions.question: Does the policy table's 'Decision metric' row, which explicitly names 'labeled rating share', provide sufficient public evidence to resolve the conflict between the printed percentage labels (Design 52%) and the y-axis 'Value' positions (Quality ~60) in favor of the labels?

Are the y-axis 'Value' positions for all six categories (Quality, Price, Design, Support, Delivery, Other) accurately captured in the current observation set to fully support the axis-based reading in base_c2?

counterquestions.summary: Inspected the chart and the initial argument set. The set correctly identifies the visible conflict between the printed percentage labels (Design 52% is highest) and the y-axis 'Value' scale (Quality ~60 is highest). The public task's policy table explicitly names 'labeled rating share' as the decision metric, which strongly supports the label-based reading (base_c1) but the initial set leaves this as an open condition. The observation set for the axis-based reading (base_c2) is incomplete, missing the y-axis positions for Price, Delivery, and Other. The option constraint (base_c3) is correctly noted but does not resolve the primary conflict.
